text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. Most APIs communicate through HTTP requests, where your application sends data to a server and receives a response. The response is usually formatted as JSON, a lightweight and easy-to-read data format. Before you can access an API, you often need authentication, such as an API key or token, to prove your identity. It is also important to respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make within a certain time. Finally, always include error handling in your code, so your application can respond properly when something goes wrong.
